items.title: Melaka polls: BN, Perikatan pledge RM30b investments, free water and no quit rent hike in joint manifesto
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 6 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) today launched a joint manifesto for the 16th Melaka state election. State BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto, themed “Membina Masa Depan Melaka, Memakmurkan Negara”, outlines 113 initiatives focusing on the cost of living, income, housing and the future of families. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Chief Minister, said BN had fulfilled up to 97 per cent of the pledges made in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka state election in 2021.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN leaders confident of delivering joint manifesto pledges
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional leaders are confident that their joint manifesto for the Melaka election is realistic, achievable and focused on the people's needs. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the manifesto had been carefully drawn up by strategists from both coalitions to ensure its pledges could be fulfilled. He said PN had appointed four to five strategists to work with their BN counterparts on drafting the manifesto.

items.title: Bursa directed Zetrix AI to address 2025 dividend non-payment, disclose material information
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia has directed Zetrix AI Bhd to address the non-payment of its 2025 final dividend by Nov 23, and disclose material information by Nov 11, to address several issues. Bursa Malaysia said the directives were issued under Paragraph 2.23 of the Main Market Listing Requirements to safeguard investor interests and ensure the timely disclosure of material information. "Bursa Malaysia takes compliance with its listing requirements seriously.

items.title: Three killed in two separate crashes along North-South Expressway
items.summary: Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the first accident occurred at 12.16pm when the couple died after their motorcycle was involved in a three-vehicle collision at KM114.4 northbound, near Tikam Batu. He said the crash was believed to have occurred when a Perodua Bezza carrying a married couple stopped on the emergency lane to change drivers before re-entering the left lane and colliding with two motorcycles. Hanyan said the rider and pillion rider of the other motorcycle, a Keeway XDV180 EVO, aged 18 and 15 respectively, were seriously injured.

items.title: Indonesia presses ahead with equity market reforms after MSCI downgrade warning
items.summary: LONDON: Indonesia is accelerating reforms aimed at addressing the equity market concerns that prompted index provider MSCI to threaten its emerging-market status and remove it from indexes tracked by funds, Investment Minister Rosan Roeslani told Reuters. MSCI froze some index changes over opaque share ownership and suspected coordinated trading, warning in October it could relegate Southeast Asia's largest economy to "standalone market" status, potentially prompting investor outflows. Rosan said the government planned to begin divesting stakes in state-owned entities next year, through IPOs or private placements.

items.title: Melaka polls: Najib house arrest issue will not affect PN campaign
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The issue surrounding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest will not affect Perikatan Nasional's campaign in the Melaka election. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the matter concerned Najib's constitutional rights, which must be respected regardless of political affiliation. He said every Malaysian convicted of an offence had the right to seek a royal pardon under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Cabinet clears move to transfer scheduled waste powers to Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Cabinet has approved an amendment order that paves the way for Sarawak to assume legislative powers over scheduled waste management from the Federal Government. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, had agreed to a memorandum from the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry on the order. Fahmi said the amendment was an important step towards suspending the enforcement of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 in Sarawak.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN unveils cradle-to-grave welfare measures
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A range of welfare measures, from savings incentives for newborns to funeral assistance, forms part of the social agenda in the joint Barisan Nasional–Perikatan Nasional election manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today. The manifesto outlines financial assistance at various stages of life for the state's 1.06 million residents. The manifesto also includes state-funded funeral assistance.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan warns heavy vehicle drivers to check blind spots as Deepavali traffic builds
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — Drivers of heavy vehicles using highways in Negeri Sembilan are reminded to be more mindful of blind spots and to ensure their surroundings are clear before changing lanes, in order to prevent accidents especially during the upcoming Deepavali festive season. Negeri Sembilan Road Transport Department (RTD) director Jasyindar Singh Sihdu said blind spots on heavy vehicles are a frequent cause of accidents, often occurring when drivers fail to check their side mirrors thoroughly, meanwhile, smaller vehicles following too closely also face significant risks. He noted that areas in the state with high concentrations of heavy vehicle traffic include Kilometre 269 and KM 258 of the PLUS Highway, as well as the roads connecting Ulu Bendul–Terachi, Seremban–Tampin, Seremban–Lukut, Batang Benar–Nilai, Gemencheh and the Bahau–Rompin road.

items.title: Mother jailed 5 years for abusing daughter; husband denies 4 rape charges
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A mother was sentenced to five years in prison for abusing her 9-year-old daughter, while her husband pleaded not guilty to four charges of raping the child. During the proceedings, a video showing the mother abusing the girl, recorded by a complainant, was played in court. The mother was sentenced to five years' imprisonment, effective from Oct 22, the date of her arrest, and fined RM10,000.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN pledges 25,000 affordable homes, 25,000 job opportunities
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A target of 25,000 affordable homes and 25,000 job opportunities over five years are among the key economic pledges in the joint Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today. It also committed to creating 25,000 job opportunities, alongside one-off technical training grants for youths from B40 households pursuing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) certifications. "For young people entering the workforce, we offer 25,000 employment opportunities," he said.

items.title: Microlink gets 12 month extension, RM60mil extra for advance passenger screening contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Microlink Solutions Bhd said its wholly-owned subsidiary Microlink System Sdn Bhd has secured a RM59.58 million contract extension from the Home Ministry for the Advance Passenger Screening (APS) system to be used by the Immigration Department, bringing the total contract value to RM137.92 million. The 12-month extension will run from Nov 6, 2026 to Nov 5, 2027, extending the overall contract period to 36 months from the original 24 months. "The additional scope under the extension covers continued application services for the onboarding of additional airlines, infrastructure services, software license renewals, and support and maintenance services for the APS system," said Microlink in a Bursa Malaysia filing.

items.title: Terminal Bersepadu Selatan expects 175,000 passengers over Deepavali travel period, up 20pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) is expected to receive approximately 175,000 passengers throughout this year’s Deepavali festive period, a 20 per cent increase compared to the same festive season last year. “We are also asking online ticket agents (OTAs) to send their own personnel to facilitate matters for passengers who purchase tickets through their respective platforms,” he said at a media session with Bernama at TBS here today. Shazwan said TBS also expects a total of 10,000 bus departures and more than 4,000 bus arrivals throughout the period.

items.title: Melaka polls: Free water, ambulance services among BN-PN pledges
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Monthly water subsidies and free ambulance services are among the key pledges in the joint Barisan Nasional–Perikatan Nasional (BN–PN) election manifesto unveiled at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today. For parents facing examination-related expenses, the coalition also pledged free tuition classes for all Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) candidates in Melaka. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the pledges were aimed at easing household expenses related to utilities, housing, healthcare and children's education, and providing financial relief to the people.

items.title: Man dies after falling from 22nd floor
items.summary: Johor Baru Selatan district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police received an emergency call about the incident about 7.30am. He said the victim was found unconscious before an ambulance from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) arrived at the scene. Azrul Hisham said preliminary investigations indicated that the victim had fallen from the building's 22nd floor.

items.title: Ringgit slips against US dollar amid global risk-off sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed lower against the US dollar on Friday, weighed down by a broad risk-off sentiment across global markets amid renewed selling pressure in the semiconductor sector. At 6pm, the local currency slipped to 4.0565/0610 versus the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0445/0490. SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit faced pressure as investors turned cautious amid heightened uncertainty in global markets.

items.title: Six MACC strategic communications officers receive IPRM accreditation
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Six officers from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Strategic Communications Division (BKS) have received the Accreditation in Public Relations (APR) award from the Institute of Public Relations Malaysia (IPRM). The MACC said in a statement that all six recipients completed their accreditation requirements, which included passing and executing a public relations (PR) case study or research publication, attending an interview session, and completing documentation. Meanwhile, Information Department (JaPen) director-general Erwin Khairul Ahmad said in the same statement that the IPRM continues to play an important role in strengthening the public relations profession in Malaysia since its establishment in 1962.

items.title: Lee Yeow Seng steps down from IOI to focus on IOI Properties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Corp Bhd has announced the resignation of Datuk Lee Yeow Seng as its non-independent non-executive director, effective Nov 6, to focus on his leadership responsibilities at IOI Properties Group Bhd. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, IOI Corp said Lee's resignation would allow him to concentrate on advancing IOI Properties' strategic priorities and creating long-term value for shareholders. Lee, 47, is the brother of IOI Corp group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Lee Yeow Chor.

items.title: Bright light seen in Malaysian airspace linked to Nasa satellite re-entry, no debris found, says Mosti
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — The Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti), through the Space Authority Division (BPAngkasa), confirmed receiving preliminary information on reports of bright light sightings in Malaysian airspace over several areas on Wednesday night (November 4). In a statement today, Mosti said the sightings were also linked to the re-entry of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (Nasa) Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory satellite. Mosti added that active monitoring is being conducted by BPAngkasa in collaboration with relevant agencies.

items.title: TRC Synergy-CCCC-UFUK Semarak JV lands RM2.69bil Penang LRT works contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TRC Synergy Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary TRC Construction Sdn Bhd (TRC) and its joint venture (JV) comprising China Communications Construction Company Ltd (CCCC) and Ufuk Semarak Sdn Bhd (UFUK) (CCCC-TRC-UFUK JV) secures RM2.69 billion Penang Light Rail Transit (LRT) project works contract worth RM2.69 billion. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the construction company said the contract entails the design, construction, and completion of a sea-crossing viaduct, including spans for navigation channels, an elevated station, and other associated works from Macallum to Penang Sentral. Yesterday, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) announced the award of the RM2.69 billion Civil Main Contract 2 Package (CMC2) to CCCC-TRC-UFUK for the Penang LRT's cross-sea extension linking Penang Island to the mainland.

items.title: Malaysia's flood insurance gap leaves households exposed to billions in losses
items.summary: General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM) chief executive officer Chua Kim Soon said many households and vehicle owners remained inadequately insured despite the increasing frequency and impact of extreme weather events. He said East Malaysia had the lowest flood insurance coverage, with only 21 per cent of fire and motor insurance policies carrying flood extensions. Chua said the insurance gap was also evident across Asia, where floods accounted for more than 50 per cent of economic losses caused by natural disasters, estimated at US$31 billion (RM125.816 billion), but only about five per cent of those losses were insured.

items.title: MISC leads RM4bil joint bid with EPF, Yinson Legacy to privatise Yinson
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MISC Bhd, together with Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund Board (EPF) had launched a privatisation bid for Yinson Holdings Bhd through a members' scheme of arrangement valued at approximately RM4.03 billion. The transaction is being undertaken by a consortium comprising MISC and its indirect wholly owned unit MISC OBU Holdings (L) Pte Ltd (MOHPL), Yinson Legacy and its shareholder and Yinson's group executive chairman Lim Han Weng, EPF's wholly owned vehicle Kwasa Layar Sdn Bhd, and acquisition vehicle MY Offshore Holdings Sdn Bhd (MYOHSB). Upon completion, MYOHSB will own 100 per cent of Yinson.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN uses 2021 manifesto record as benchmark for new pledges
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka Barisan Nasional has fulfilled 97 per cent of the pledges made in its manifesto for the 2021 state election. State BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the achievement would serve as a benchmark for the state government in assessing the effectiveness and delivery of its future commitments to the people. The caretaker Melaka chief minister said the achievement demonstrated the state government's commitment to ensuring that election promises were not merely political pledges but translated into tangible results through transparent and accountable governance.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 6, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended 1.18 per cent, or 19.28 points lower on Friday, weighed down by losses in Press Metal Aluminium and YTL Power International. All sectors closed in negative territory, with the technology sector emerging as the worst performer. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Nestcon bags RM161mil serviced apartment work in Gombak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestcon Bhd has secured a RM161 million contract from B.U. Developments Sdn Bhd to construct a 36-storey serviced apartment building in Bandar Baru Ulu Kelang, Gombak, Selangor. The contract involves the main building works for the serviced apartment development, with construction commencing on Nov 2.

items.title: AGC says Najib’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) says the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest should be temporarily postponed pending legal clarification on the interpretation of his conditional pardon and the effect of a High Court order issued today. However, the AGC said two possible interpretations had arisen over whether payment of the fine meant Najib’s prison sentence in the SRC International case remained in force or was considered completed. Under the second interpretation, payment of the fine would allow the pardon to take full effect, meaning the entire sentence for the SRC International case, including the prison term, would be considered completed.

items.title: Muhyiddin calls for clarity on rules governing Najib's house arrest
items.summary: MELAKA: The government has been urged to clarify the rules governing house arrest for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to ensure the public understands its legal basis and the restrictions imposed. Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said it remained unclear whether house arrest was governed by specific regulations similar to those imposed on prison inmates. "As far as I remember, there is no specific law governing the regulations for house arrest.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN-PN manifesto outlines 113 initiatives for state
items.summary: MELAKA: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional have unveiled a joint manifesto for the Melaka election, outlining 113 initiatives to spur development and improve the well-being of the state's people. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the initiatives included free water, 25,000 affordable homes and 25,000 job opportunities over the next five years. He said the manifesto covered housing, the cost of living, education, employment, public welfare, economic growth and the state's development needs.

items.title: Maybank IB allotted 225mil shares in Big Caring IPO for price stabilisation measures
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Investment Bank has announced that it has been granted an over-allotment option comprising up to 225.15 million shares for the upcoming initial public offering (IPO) of Big Caring Group Bhd (BCG). In a Bursa Malaysia filing by BCG, Maybank IB stated that BCG's shares may be subject to stabilising action following the IPO. The stabilisation period will officially commence on Nov 19, the listing date of BCG on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia.

items.title: Najib taken for scheduled dental examination after leaving Kajang Prison, Anthony Loke says
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has yet to return home after leaving Kajang Prison today, as he was taken to a dental clinic for a scheduled examination, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said. Loke, who earlier announced his resignation as transport minister, said he received the information from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. “The Home Minister had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home.

items.title: MARC downgrades YNH's RM700mil sukuk on weak cash flow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has downgraded YNH Property Bhd's RM700 million Sukuk Wakalah programme rating to BIS from BBIS and placed it on MARCWatch Negative, citing weakened liquidity and heightened refinancing and repayment risks. The rating agency said the downgrade reflects YNH's weak internal cash flow generation, continued reliance on asset disposals to meet financial obligations and limited earnings visibility. As at Oct 27, YNH's reserve account stood at RM54.4 million, RM6.8 million below the required RM61.2 million, resulting in a technical default, the rating agency said.

items.title: Penang committed to sustainable, well-regulated pig farming, says state exco
items.summary: TASEK GELUGOR, Nov 6 — The Penang state government is committed to ensuring that the pig farming industry in the state continues to be managed in an orderly and sustainable manner through more systematic management, close monitoring and effective enforcement of regulations. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye said this approach would allow the industry to continue operating and growing in line with legal requirements and standards without compromising environmental sustainability. “The state government has never shied away from acknowledging the pollution caused by improper management of pig farming waste in the past; instead, we have taken corrective measures to ensure the issue is addressed comprehensively.

items.title: Financially vulnerable Malaysians targeted for recruitment as drug mules, police say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Individuals with financial difficulties, especially those from Sarawak and Pahang, have been targeted by international drug smuggling rings to be recruited as drug mules. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicate’s activities were exposed following the arrest of four individuals, including the foreign mastermind, in Brickfields here yesterday. “Two pairs of shoes and 450 grams of cocaine believed destined for two drug mules were also seized,” he said at a media conference here today, adding the the local men were arrested under Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.

items.title: Genetec exits battery JV with Citaglobal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genetec Technology Bhd is exiting its battery energy storage joint venture (JV) with Citaglobal Bhd, by disposing of its 50 per cent stake in Citaglobal Genetec BESS Sdn Bhd (CG BESS) to its former partner. The stake, which comprises 250,000 ordinary shares, will be acquired by Citaglobal New Energy Sdn Bhd (Citaglobal NE), a subsidiary of Citaglobal. The transaction also includes a proposed debt transfer, where Genetec will transfer to Citaglobal NE all rights and interests regarding an intercompany balance of RM2.24 million that is currently owed by CG BESS to Genetec.

items.title: Zahid, Turkish higher education council chief discuss stronger TVET cooperation
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today received a courtesy call from Turkish Higher Education Council (YOK) president Prof Dr Erol Ozvar. Zahid said the meeting was also aimed at reviewing memoranda of understanding (MoUs), cooperation agreements and technical agreements signed between higher education institutions in Malaysia and Turkiye. "We already have close cooperation between universities in Turkiye and Malaysia.

items.title: Malaysia declares 69 items National Heritage, from ‘mi kolok’ to Dewan Rakyat mace
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — A total of 69 heritage items have been recognised as National Heritage 2026, including uthappam , mi kolok and kek lapis , popular foods that reflect Malaysia’s cultural diversity, Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said. In a statement marking the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026, he said 39 heritage items had been declared to date, while a further 30 would be gazetted later. “The total includes heritage items recognised as part of efforts to preserve and protect the nation’s heritage, covering tangible and intangible heritage as well as recipients of the Living National Heritage Award (WAKOH),” he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Najib's house arrest should be suspended pending legal review, says A-GC
items.summary: The A-GC, in a statement, said Najib's existing detention status should be maintained until the legal issues surrounding the pardon and the High Court's order for his release were resolved. The statement came hours after Umno settled Najib's RM50 million fine and the High Court issued an order of discharge on payment of the fine, directing his immediate release while requiring him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028. "First, the payment of the RM50 million fine only fulfils the fine component of the sentence, while the prison sentence for the SRC International case remains in force until Aug 23, 2028.

items.title: OPR stays at 2.75pc as Bank Negara sees no need to tighten monetary policy, says governor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent reflects its assessment that the rate remains consistent with price stability outlook and sustainable economic growth, said Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour. Abdul Rasheed said global growth demonstrated resilience, supported by factors such as the continued expansion of technology-related investments and strong demand associated with the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. He said Malaysia’s economy demonstrated resilience in sustaining growth, with the third-quarter (3Q) advance estimate recording a 5.3 per cent expansion and average growth for the first three quarters reaching 5.6 per cent.

items.title: 69 items named National Heritage 2026, from traditional foods to historic artefacts
items.summary: In a statement marking the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026, he said the list reflects Malaysia's cultural diversity. "The total includes heritage items recognised as part of efforts to preserve and protect the nation's heritage, covering tangible and intangible heritage as well as recipients of the Living National Heritage Award," he said. Sixteen heritage objects were also accorded National Heritage status.

items.title: Teacher acquitted of three sexual assault charges involving students
items.summary: TAWAU: The Sessions Court acquitted and discharged a teacher of three counts of sexual assault involving three female students three years ago. The court also ordered that Sanyzam's bail money be returned. The investigating officer also failed to inspect or retrieve an "MMI" book mentioned by one of the victims in her testimony.

items.title: BN manifesto launch: PN shows support, signals united front for Melaka polls
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A sea of blue and green filled the grounds of the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) this evening as supporters and party machinery from Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) gathered for the launch of BN's manifesto for the 16th Melaka state election. Supporters carrying BN's dacing flags and PN banners began arriving as early as 3pm, filling parking areas and surrounding access roads around MITC. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh unveiled the election manifesto at 5pm.

items.title: Transport Minister Anthony Loke resigns as Najib returns home to begin house arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 6 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook has announced his resignation after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. Loke said his stance on the matter had not changed and that his resignation would take effect the moment Najib arrives home. “However, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had informed me that Najib had not yet been allowed to return home,” he said.

items.title: Zahid reminds Loke of pledge to resign from Cabinet post if Najib is released for house arrest today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Transport Minister Anthony Loke to step down today if former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is released following the settlement of his RM50 million fine. Zahid said Loke must honour his pledge, according to a New Straits Times report. “He must do it immediately if Datuk Seri Najib is released today.”

items.title: MetMalaysia forecasts continuous rain in Kelantan, Terengganu from Sunday to Nov 11
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Continuous rain is expected in several parts of Kelantan and Terengganu from Sunday until Nov 11, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the affected areas in Kelantan include Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok and Pasir Puteh. In Terengganu, continuous rain is expected to affect Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu, Marang and Hulu Terengganu, he said.

items.title: PM disagrees with Umno’s RM50m fine payment for Najib, but respects legal process
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed disagreement with Umno’s decision to pay the RM50 million fine on behalf of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, stressing that corruption and abuse of power must not be taken lightly in the name of friendship. Anwar said personal ties and goodwill towards Najib should not create the impression that corruption and abuse of power involving billions of ringgit could be overlooked. While we have a sense of friendship with Datuk Seri Najib, it must not give the public the impression that corruption involving billions of ringgit can simply be overlooked.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia assessing impact of US midterm election results, including tariffs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The government is examining the short and medium-term impacts across various aspects following political developments in the United States (US), where the Republican Party suffered a defeat in the midterm elections on Tuesday. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed in depth during today’s Cabinet meeting and Malaysia will continue to monitor the situation, including potential implications regarding the implementation of reciprocal tariffs. “…however, our relations with the current administration, the existing government, as well as both incumbent and newly elected members of Congress including the House of Representatives will continue,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at Taman Kosas Mosque, near here, today.

items.title: Cabinet approves transfer of scheduled waste management powers to Sarawak under MA63
items.summary: Madani government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the memorandum, submitted by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), was agreed upon at today’s Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The move, he said, would also prevent overlapping jurisdiction between the federal and Sarawak governments. Fahmi also said the transfer of federal legislative powers in environmental matters to Sabah and Sarawak would be implemented in phases, beginning with scheduled waste management, he added.

items.title: Najib exits Kajang Prison to serve out SRC sentence under house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Malaysia’s former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak left prison on Friday after paying a fine that allows him to serve the rest of his sentence at home, an AFP reporter saw. Najib, 73, was whisked from Kajang Prison in a silver car followed by a convoy of vehicles, according to an AFP reporter at the scene. MORE TO COME

items.title: Teo Nie Ching urges govt agencies to conduct cybersecurity audits amid rising hacking threats
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 6 — All government agencies must conduct cybersecurity audits to identify vulnerabilities in their respective digital systems and infrastructure amid heightened hacking threats linked to developments in international conflicts. Teo said efforts to strengthen cybersecurity should also extend to the private sector, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and associations, particularly those that rely on the internet and store data online. She said all organisations, particularly those operating critical infrastructure such as hospitals and banking systems, should allocate dedicated funds for cybersecurity audits.

items.title: Selangor to review approved projects, tighten flood mitigation requirements in high-risk areas
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Nov 6 — The Selangor state government will order a review of previously approved development projects to ensure that flood mitigation systems are implemented in high-risk areas. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari saId this measure is part of the state government’s efforts to reduce flood risks and prevent a recurrence of such incidents in the affected areas. Amirudin added that the state government has also identified several other issues contributing to flooding in areas such as Johan Setia, Parit Mahang, Bukit Kuching, and Bukit Hijau.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Customs seizes RM2.56m in cigarettes, liquor and smuggled goods
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 6 — The Negeri Sembilan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department crippled smuggling activities in two raids on Oct 26, seizing cigarettes, liquor and other goods with a total value of RM2.56 million, including duties. Its director, Jamal Paiman, said the seizures by the Enforcement Division involved various items worth RM359,271, with duties amounting to RM2.2 million. He said the items seized comprised 3,008,200 sticks of cigarettes of various brands, 2,910.64 litres of liquor, 221 electrical appliances and a packaging machine.

items.title: High Court orders Najib’s house arrest after Umno settles RM50m fine payment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The High Court has issued a house arrest order for Datuk Seri Najib Razak after his RM50 million fine in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was settled today. Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, a member of Najib’s legal team, confirmed the payment was made by Umno to the High Court registry this morning, according to The Star . “As of this morning, the RM50 million fine before Najib has been paid by Umno to the High Court,” he said during the press conference.

items.title: Johor Domestic Trade Ministry logs 2,373 offences, RM11.6m in seizures in price control crackdown
items.summary: Johor KPDN director Lilis Saslinda Pornomo said that of this total, 1,774 cases involved offences under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011. She said among the offences were the failure to display clear price tags or price lists for goods or services, selling controlled items above the stipulated maximum price and raising prices or profiteering in an unreasonable manner. Lilis Saslinda said the ministry also detected 54 other offences under the Trademarks Act 2019, the Trade Descriptions Act 2011, the Copyright Act 1987 and the Hire-Purchase Act 1967.

items.title: ‘Payment completed’: Umno settles Najib’s RM50m fine, paving way for house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court for the RM50 million fine imposed on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, the party announced today. “Umno has completed all payment processes to the Kuala Lumpur High Court this morning,” he said. “Umno hereby officially closes the special Najib Razak Solidarity Fund account and no longer needs crowdfunding for this purpose,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast for six states and Putrajaya until 2pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across six states and the Federal Territory of Putrajaya, expected to last until 2pm today. The warning, issued in a statement at noon today, covers Pahang (Kuantan and Rompin), Selangor (Sepang, Kuala Langat, Klang, Petaling and Kuala Selangor), Putrajaya, and Johor (Kota Tinggi and Mersing). In Sarawak, the affected areas are Mukah (Mukah, Dalat and Matu), Bintulu (Tatau and Bintulu), Sibu, Kapit (Song), Sri Aman (Lubok Antu) and Betong (Betong).

items.title: Najib’s lawyer, special officer enter KL Court Complex as RM50m fine payment speculation mounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A member of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s legal team arrived at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex in Jalan Duta today at noon, according to a New Straits Times report. Lawyer Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee was seen entering the complex as speculation grew that the RM50 million fine could be settled, potentially allowing the former prime minister to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest. Lutfi and Farhan were later seen entering the High Court Criminal Registry office together.

items.title: Police cordon off Najib’s Jalan Langgak Duta residence amid speculation of possible return
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — Police have tightened security at the entrance to Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here this morning, amid speculation that the former prime minister may return to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. Berita Harian reported that Najib may be permitted to return home after settling the required payment. Anuar Bakri said officers had laid police tape to keep unauthorised individuals away from Najib’s home.

items.title: Legal disputes cast doubt on year-end Petronas-Sarawak settlement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 6 — A year-end settlement between Sarawak and Petronas is not possible despite Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg expressing confidence that a deal could be reached before the end of the year, a political analyst said. “You cannot get an agreement while these court cases are happening unless Petronas withdraws, or both sides go to the courts and say they want to settle out of court,” Chin said. He had earlier said only administrative and commercial issues remained unresolved.

items.title: Three more held over fatal machete attack in Teluk Intan
items.summary: Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the three suspects were aged between their 30s and 40s. “Two foreign men were arrested in the early hours of Nov 4 and remanded on the same day until Nov 11. On Nov 4, Chua said preliminary investigations found that the 48-year-old victim had been attacked by three men armed with machetes.

items.title: MyJPJ data not shared with insurance partner Nile Tech, says MOT
items.summary: In a written response published on the Parliament website, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) clarified that the insurance renewal service featured in MyJPJ serves merely as a link, directing users to the Nile Tech portal to complete their transactions. “When the link is selected, users are redirected from the MyJPJ application to the Nile Tech portal. All insurance renewal processes and transactions take place on that portal.
